passages.text: NOTE 9 — DEBT INSTRUMENTS Debt instruments, excluding finance leases, which are discussed in Note 15 — Leases, as of December 31, 2025 and 2024 consisted of the following: December 31, 2025 2024 (in millions) Asset-based financing: Floor plan facility $ 58 $ 67 Financing of beneficial interests in securitizations 374 354 Real estate financing 485 485 Transportation fleet financing 23 — Total asset-based financing 940 906 Senior Secured Notes (1) 3,929 4,358 Senior Unsecured Notes 107 205 Total debt 4,976 5,469 Less: current portion ( 211 ) ( 302 ) Less: unamortized debt issuance costs (2) ( 36 ) ( 46 ) Plus: unamortized premium (3) 18 27 Total included in long-term debt, net $ 4,747 $ 5,148 (1) Includes zero and $ 105 million of accrued paid-in-kind ("PIK") interest as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. Accrued PIK interest increases the principal amount of Senior Secured Notes on each semi-annual interest payment date. (2) The unamortized debt issuance costs related to long-term debt are presented as a reduction of the carrying amount of the corresponding liabilities on the accompanying consolidated balance sheets. Unamortized debt issuance costs related to revolving debt arrangements are presented within other assets on the accompanying consolidated balance sheets and not included here. (3) The unamortized premium relates to a portion of the notes exchange offers completed in September 2023 which were accounted for as a debt modification. Short-Term Revolving Facilities Floor Plan Facility The Company previously entered into a floor plan facility with Ally to finance its vehicle inventory, which was secured by Carvana LLC's vehicle inventory, general intangibles, accounts receivable, and finance receivables (as amended, the "Floor Plan Facility"). On September 1, 2023, the Company amended the Floor Plan Facility in connection with the issuance of the Senior Secured Notes (as defined below) to provide for an additional exclusive grant of collateral over certain deposit accounts and the cash on deposit in those accounts in favor of the lender and to amend certain other affirmative and negative covenants. The Company further amended the Floor Plan Facility on April 29, 2025 to renew the line of credit at $ 1.5 billion until April 30, 2027. Under the amendment, the interest rate on the Floor Plan Facility was reduced to (i) a prime rate minus 0.70 % when amounts drawn under the Floor Plan Facility are less than 25 % of the then current inventory balance, (ii) a prime rate minus 0.50 % when amounts drawn under the Floor Plan Facility are 25 % or more but less than 50 % of the then current inventory balance, or (iii) a prime rate plus 0.10 % when amounts drawn under the Floor Plan Facility are 50 % or more of the then current inventory balance. The Floor Plan Facility also requires monthly interest payments and restricted cash requirements on a sliding scale whereby at least 5 % of the total principal amount owed to the lender is required to be held as restricted cash if amounts drawn are under 25 % of the then current inventory balance, increasing to 12.5 % to be held as restricted cash if amounts drawn are between 25 % and 49.99 % of

passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion should be read in conjunction with Part I, including matters set forth in the "Risk Factors" section of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, and our financial statements and notes thereto included in Part II, Item 8 "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data," of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Except when stated otherwise, we present the discussion in Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations on a consolidated basis. Overview Carvana is the leading e-commerce platform for buying and selling used cars. We are transforming the used car buying and selling experience by giving consumers what they want - a wide selection, great value and quality, transparent pricing, and a simple, no pressure transaction. Each element of our business, from inventory procurement to fulfillment and overall ease of the online transaction, has been built for this singular purpose. See Part I, Item 1 - "Business" for a detailed description and discussion of the Company's business. Refer to " Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations " in Part II, Item 7 of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 filed with the SEC on February 19, 2025 for discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 compared to the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023. Retail Vehicle Unit Sales Since launching to customers in Atlanta, Georgia in January 2013, we have experienced rapid growth in sales through our website www.carvana.com. During the year ended December 31, 2025, the number of vehicles we sold to retail customers increased by 43.3% to 596,641, compared to 416,348 in the year ended December 31, 2024. We continue to view the number of vehicles we sell to retail customers as the most important long-term measure of our performance, and we expect to continue to focus on building a scalable platform to efficiently increase our retail units sold. This focus on retail units sold is motivated by several factors: • Retail units sold enable multiple revenue streams, including the sale of the vehicle itself, the sale of finance receivables originated to finance the vehicle, complementary products, and the sale of vehicles acquired from customers. • Retail units sold are the primary driver of customer referrals and repeat sales. Each time we sell a vehicle to a new customer, that customer may refer future customers and can become a repeat buyer in the future. • Retail units sold allow us to benefit from economies of scale due to our centralized online sales model. We believe our model provides meaningful operating leverage in acquisition, reconditioning, transport, customer service, and delivery. We continue to prioritize efficient growth in retail units sold, absent any material changes in macroeconomic conditions. To prioritize growth, we are pursuing investments in technology and infrastructure, while simultaneously maintaining our focus on efficiency gains and profitability. credit_strengths.text: Carvana's revenue and operating income have scaled rapidly, with operating margin now near the low double digits, though still below the sector median. This earnings trajectory reflects operating leverage in reconditioning, logistics and online retail, supporting internal cash generation and reducing reliance on external funding for working capital.

Liquidity is substantial, with cash exceeding current liabilities and a current ratio well above the sector median. Free cash flow covers a meaningful slice of debt, and the Altman Z double-prime zone is Safe. This buffer supports near-term maturities and inventory financing needs.

key_risks.text: The debt note shows a large secured note stack with a modest unsecured tail, and the floor plan facility is secured by vehicle inventory and receivables. A refinancing or covenant event could impair flexibility, especially if used-car demand or inventory values weaken, constraining asset-based borrowing capacity.

Risk factors flag macroeconomic slowdown, tariffs and used-car market volatility, which could pressure retail unit sales and margins. Because the business model depends on vehicle sourcing and consumer financing, adverse conditions may reduce operating cash flow and tighten interest coverage, which already sits below the sector median.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating cash flow covers interest expense multiple times, but interest coverage remains below the sector median. Free cash flow to debt is modest relative to peers, indicating that debt service depends on sustained earnings and working capital discipline rather than a large cash-flow cushion.

The maturity profile is weighted to later years, with the next twelve months representing a small share of total debt. This reduces near-term refinancing pressure, but the concentration in year five and beyond means the company must maintain market access or generate sufficient cash to repay or refinance the secured notes.

overall_credit_view.text: Carvana's credit profile is intermediate: strong revenue growth, positive free cash flow and ample liquidity offset leverage that is elevated relative to sector medians. The absence of a depreciation and amortization tag prevents a precise EBITDA-based leverage calculation, a material gap for assessing debt capacity and covenant headroom.

Analyst judgement: the company should continue to deleverage if retail unit growth and operating margins hold, but a demand downturn or tariff-driven cost pressure could stall that trajectory. The secured debt structure and back-loaded maturities warrant monitoring, though current liquidity and cash generation provide a reasonable cushion.

credit_strengths.text: Carvana 的收入及經營利潤快速增長，經營利潤率現已接近低雙位數，但仍低於行業中位數。此盈利軌跡反映在翻新、物流及線上零售方面的經營槓桿，支持內部現金產生並減少對外部資金作為營運資金的依賴。
流動性充裕，現金超過流動負債，流動比率遠高於行業中位數。自由現金流覆蓋相當部分的債務，而 Altman Z 雙質數區域為 Safe。此緩衝支持短期到期債務及存貨融資需求。

key_risks.text: 債務票據顯示大量有抵押票據堆疊，僅有少量無抵押尾部，而 floor plan 融資以車輛存貨及應收賬款作抵押。再融資或契約事件可能損害靈活性，尤其若二手車需求或存貨價值轉弱，將限制基於資產的借款能力。
風險因素標示宏觀經濟放緩、關稅及二手車市場波動，可能對零售單位銷量及利潤率構成壓力。由於業務模式依賴車輛採購及消費者融資，不利條件可能減少經營現金流並收緊利息覆蓋率，而該覆蓋率已低於行業中位數。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 經營現金流覆蓋利息支出數倍，但利息覆蓋率仍低於行業中位數。自由現金流對債務的比率相對同業適度，表明債務償付依賴持續盈利及營運資金紀律，而非龐大現金流緩衝。
到期結構偏重於較後年份，未來十二個月佔總債務比例較小。這減少短期再融資壓力，但集中於第五年及之後意味著公司必須維持市場准入或產生足夠現金以償還或再融資有抵押票據。

overall_credit_view.text: Carvana 的信貸狀況屬中等：強勁收入增長、正自由現金流及充裕流動性抵銷了相對行業中位數偏高的槓桿。缺乏折舊及攤銷標籤阻礙了精確的 EBITDA 槓桿計算，這對評估債務能力及契約空間構成重大缺口。
分析師判斷：若零售單位增長及經營利潤率保持，公司應繼續去槓桿，但需求下滑或關稅驅動的成本壓力可能令該軌跡停滯。有抵押債務結構及後置到期值得監察，儘管當前流動性及現金產生提供合理緩衝。
